questions.prompt: File systems and device drivers run as user processes and talk through the kernel by messages.
Everything below the system-call interface is one big program in one address space.
Each part may use only the services of parts strictly below it, down to the hardware at level 0.
Written for minimum size, not divided into modules, and applications can call the BIOS directly.
A small core kernel links in drivers and file systems as needed, and they call each other directly inside the kernel.
Which structure has the HIGHEST communication overhead between OS services?
Which structure lets a crashed device driver be restarted like any other program while the system keeps running?
Which structure is easiest to debug one level at a time?
A structure where modules run inside the kernel gets microkernel-like flexibility without the message-passing cost.
